You quickly mastered the skills to identify and process rare and complex botanical and alchemical samples and the proper extractions and infusions of essential oils, pollens, and other fragrant chemical compounds—natural or otherwise. Not all (dramatic) changes to one's lifestyle, calling, or ambitions are a result of social or financial decline. Some are simply decided upon. Regardless of your motivation or incentive for change, you have accepted that a comfortable life of research, science and business is—at least for now—a part of your past.

**Tool Proficiencies.** Alchemist's supplies, herbalism kit

**Languages.** No additional languages

**Aromas and Odors and Airs, Oh My.** Before you became an adventurer, you crafted perfumes for customers in your home town or city. When not out adventuring, you can fall back on that trade to make a living. For each week you spend practicing your profession, you can craft one of the following at half the normal cost in time and resources: 5 samples of fine perfume worth 10 gp each, 2 vials of acid, or 1 vial of parfum toxique worth 50 gp. As an action, you can throw a vial of parfum toxique up to 20 feet, shattering it on impact. Make a ranged attack against a creature or object, treating the parfum as an improvised weapon. On a hit, the target takes 1d6 poison damage and is poisoned until the end of its next turn.
gear: Herbalism kit, a leather satchel containing perfume recipes, research notes, and chemical and botanical samples; 1d4 metal or crystal (shatter-proof) perfume bottles, a set of fine clothes, and a silk purse containing 10 gp

name: Scoundrel
desc:
You were brought up in a poor neighborhood in a crowded town or city. You may have been lucky enough to have a leaky roof over your head, or perhaps you grew up sleeping in doorways or on the rooftops. Either way, you didn't have it easy, and you lived by your wits. While never a hardened criminal, you fell in with the wrong crowd, or you ended up in trouble for stealing food from an orange cart or clean clothes from a washing line. You're no stranger to the city watch in your hometown and have outwitted or outrun them many times.

**Tool Proficiencies.** One type of gaming set, thieves' tools

**Languages.** No additional languages

**Urban Explorer.** You are familiar with the layout and rhythms of towns and cities. When you arrive in a new city, you can quickly locate places to stay, where to buy good quality gear, and other facilities. You can shake off pursuers when you are being chased through the streets or across the rooftops. You have a knack for leading pursuers into a crowded market filled with stalls piled high with breakable merchandise, or down a narrow alley just as a dung cart is coming in the other direction.
gear: A bag of 1,000 ball bearings, a pet monkey wearing a tiny fez, a set of common clothes, and a pouch containing 10 gp

name: Sentry
desc:
In your youth, the defense of the city, the community, the caravan, or your patron was how you earned your coin. You might have been trained by an old, grizzled city watchman, or you might have been pressed into service by the local magistrate for your superior skills, size, or intellect. However you came to the role, you excelled at defending others. You have a nose for trouble, a keen eye for spotting threats, a strong arm to back it up, and you are canny enough to know when to act. Most importantly, though, you were a peace officer or a protector and not a member of an army which might march to war.

**Specialization**
Each person or location that hires a sentry comes with its own set of unique needs and responsibilities. As a sentry, you fulfilled one of these unique roles. Choose a specialization or roll a d6 and consult the table below to define your expertise as a sentry.

| d6 | Specialization |
|---|---|
| 1 | City or gate watch |
| 2 | Bodyguard or jailor |
| 3 | Caravan guard |
| 4 | Palace or judicial sentry |
| 5 | Shop guard |
| 6 | Ecclesiastical or temple guard |

**Tool Proficiencies.** One type of gaming set

**Languages.** One language of your choice

**Comrades in Arms.** The knowing look from the caravan guard to the city gatekeeper or the nod of recognition between the noble's bodyguard and the district watchman—no matter the community, city, or town, the guards share a commonality of purpose. When you arrive in a new location, you can speak briefly with the gate guards, local watch, or other community guardians to gain local knowledge. This knowledge could be information, such as the most efficient routes through the city, primary vendors for a variety of luxury goods, the best (or worst) inns and taverns, the primary criminal elements in town, or the current conflicts in the community.
gear: A set of dice or deck of cards, a shield bearing your previous employer's symbol, a set of common clothes, a hooded lantern, a signal whistle, and a belt pouch containing 10 gp

name: Trophy Hunter
desc:
You hunt the mightiest beasts in the harshest environments, claiming their pelts as trophies and returning them to settled lands for a profit or to decorate your abode. You likely were set on this path since birth, following your parents on safaris and learning from their actions, but you may have instead come to this path as an adult after being swept away by the thrill of dominating the natural world. Many big game hunters pursue their quarry purely for pleasure, as a calming avocation, but others sell their skills to the highest bidder to amass wealth and reputation as a trophy hunter.

**Tool Proficiencies.** Leatherworker's tools, vehicles (land)

**Languages.** No additional languages

**Shelter from the Storm.** You have spent years hunting in the harshest environments of the world and have seen tents blown away by gales, food stolen by hungry bears, and equipment destroyed by the elements. While traveling in the wilderness, you can find a natural location suitable to make camp by spending 1 hour searching. This location provides cover from the elements and is in some way naturally defensible, at the GM's discretion.
gear: A donkey or mule with bit and bridle, a set of cold-weather or warm-weather clothes, and a belt pouch containing 5 gp

name: Crime Syndicate Member
desc:
Whether you grew up in slum-run streets bamboozling foolish gamblers out of their fortune, or spent your youth pilfering loose coin from the pockets of less-attentive travelers, your lifestyle of deceiving-to-survive eventually drew the attention of an organized and dangerous crime syndicate. Offering protection, a modicum of kinship, and a number of useful resources to further develop your craft as a criminal, you agree to receive the syndicate’s brand and join their ranks.
You might have been working the syndicate’s lower ranks, wandering the alleys as a simple cutpurse to fill the meager coffers with wayward gold until the opportunity arose to climb the professional ladder. Or you may have become a clever actor and liar whose skill in blending in with all facets of society has made you an indispensable agent of information gathering. Perhaps your technique with a blade and swiftness of action led you to become a feared hitman for a syndicate boss, sending you on the occasional contract to snuff the life of some unfortunate soul who crossed them. Regardless, while the threat of the law is ever looming, the advantages to having a foot in such a powerful cartel can greatly outweigh the paranoia.

**Tool Proficiencies.** Your choice of one from Thieves’ Tools, Forgery Kit, or Disguise Kit.

**Languages.** Thieves’ Cant

**A Favor In Turn.** You have gained enough clout within the syndicate that you can call in a favor from your contacts, should you be close enough to a center of syndicate activity. A request for a favor can be no longer than 20 words, and is passed up the chain to an undisclosed syndicate boss for approval. This favor can take a shape up to the DM’s discretion depending on the request, with varying speeds of fulfillment: If muscle is requested, an NPC syndicate minion can temporarily aid the party. If money is needed, a small loan can be provided. If you’ve been imprisoned, they can look into breaking you free, or paying off the jailer.
The turn comes when a favor is asked to be repaid. The favor debt can be called in without warning, and many times with intended immediacy. Perhaps the player is called to commit a specific burglary without the option to decline. Maybe they must press a dignitary for a specific secret at an upcoming ball. The syndicate could even request a hit on an NPC, no questions asked or answered. The DM is to provide a debt call proportionate to the favor fulfilled. If a favor is not repaid within a reasonable period of time, membership to the crime syndicate can be revoked, and if the debt is large enough, the player may become the next hit contract to make the rounds.
gear: A set of dark common clothes including a hood, a set of tools to match your choice of tool proficiency, and a belt pouch containing 10g.

name: Elemental Warden
desc:
Away from the complex political struggles of the massive cities, you’ve instead been raised to revere and uphold the protection of the natural world, while policing, bending, and guiding the elemental powers that either foster life or destroy it. Living among smaller bands of tribal societies means you have stronger ties to your neighbors than most, and the protection of this way of life is of cardinal importance. Each elemental warden is tethered to one of the four elemental tribes and their villages. You must select one: Fire, Water, Earth, or Wind.
Your upbringing may have prepared you to be a fierce warrior, trained in combat to defend your culture and charge as protectors of the rifts. It’s possible your meditation on the balance of the elements has brought you peace of mind with strength of body as a monk. Perhaps you found strength in bending the elements yourself, joining the ranks of the powerful elemental druids. Regardless, your loyalties ultimately lie with the continued safety of your tribe, and you’ve set out to gather allies to your cause and learn more about the world around you.

**Tool Proficiencies.** Herbalism Kit

**Languages.** One of your choice.

**Elemental Harmony.** Your upbringing surrounded by such strong, wild elemental magics has attuned your senses to the very nature of their chaotic forces, enabling you to subtly bend them to your will in small amounts. You learn the _Prestidigitation_ Cantrip, but can only produce the extremely minor effects below that involve the element of your chosen elemental tribe: 
* You create an instantaneous puff of wind strong enough to blow papers off a desk, or mess up someone’s hair (Wind). 
* You instantaneously create and control a burst of flame small enough to light or snuff out a candle, a torch, or a small campfire. (Fire). 
* You instantaneously create a small rock within your hand, no larger than a gold coin, that turns to dust after a minute (Earth). 
* You instantaneously create enough hot or cold water to fill a small glass (Water).
gear: A staff, hunting gear (a shortbow with 20 arrows, or a hunting trap), a set of traveler’s clothes, a belt pouch containing 10 gp.

name: Fate-Touched
desc:
Many lives and many souls find their ways through the patterns of fate and destiny, their threads following the path meant for them, oblivious and eager to be a part of the woven essence of history meant for them. Some souls, however, glide forth with mysterious influence, their threads bending the weave around them, toward them, unknowingly guiding history itself wherever they walk. Events both magnificent and catastrophic tend to follow such individuals. These souls often become great rulers and terrible tyrants, powerful mages, religious leaders, and legendary heroes of lore. These are the fate-touched.
Few fate-touched ever become aware of their prominent nature. Outside of powerful divination magics, it’s extremely difficult to confirm one as fate-touched. There are many communities that regard the status as a terrible omen, treating a confirmed fate-touched with mistrust and fear. Others seek them as a blessing, rallying around them for guidance. Some of renown and power grow jealous, wishing to bend a fate-touched beneath their will, and some stories speak of mages of old attempting to extract or transfer the essence itself.
Players are not intended to select this background, but this is instead provided for the dungeon master to consider for one or more of their players, or perhaps a prominent NPC, as their campaign unfolds. It provides very minor mechanical benefit, but instead adds an element of lore, importance, and fate-bearing responsibility to a character within your story. Being fate-touched overlaps and co-exists with the character’s current background, only adding to their mystique. Consider it for a player character who would benefit from being put more central to the coming conflicts of your adventure, or for an NPC who may require protection as they come into their destiny. Perhaps consider a powerful villain discovering their fate-twisting nature and using it to wreak havoc. All of these possibilities and more can be explored should you choose to include a fate-touched within your campaign.

**Fortune’s Grace.** Your fate-touched essence occasionally leads surrounding events to shift in your favor. You gain 1 Luck point, as per the Lucky feat outlined within the Player’s Handbook pg 167. This luck point is used in the same fashion as the feat, and you regain this expended luck point when you finish a long rest. If you already have the Lucky feat, you add this luck point to your total for the feat.

name: Lyceum Student
desc:
You most likely came up through money or a family of social prestige somewhere in the world, as tuition at a lyceum is not inexpensive. Your interests and pursuits have brought you to the glittering halls of a place of learning, soaking in all and every lesson you can to better make your mark on the world (or at least you should be, but every class has its slackers). However, the call to adventure threatens to pull you from your studies, and now the challenge of balancing your education with the tide of destiny sweeping you away is looming.
You may have come to better research and understand the history and lore of the lands you now call home, perhaps seeking a future here at your lyceum as a professor. You could also have been drawn by the promise of prosperity in politics, learning the inner workings of government and alliances to better position yourself as a future writer of history. Perhaps you’ve discovered a knack for the arcane, coming here to focus on refining your spellcraft in the footsteps of some of the finest wizards and sorcerers in days of yore.

**Languages.** Two of your choice

**Student Privilege.** You’ve cleared enough lessons, and gained an ally or two on staff, to have access to certain chambers within the lyceum (and some other allied universities) that outsiders would not. This allows use of any Tool Kit, so long as the Tool Kit is used on the grounds of the lyceum and is not removed from its respective chamber (each tool kit is magically marked and will sound an alarm if removed). More dangerous kits and advanced crafts (such as use of a Poisoner’s Kit, or the enchanting of a magical item) might require staff supervision. You may also have access to free crafting materials and enchanting tables, so long as they are relatively inexpensive, or your argument for them is convincing (up to the staff’s approval and DM’s discretion).
gear: A set of fine clothes, a lyceum student uniform, a writing kit (small pouch with a quill, ink, folded parchment, and a small penknife), and a belt pouch containing 10g.

name: Recovered Cultist
desc:
Dark deities whisper and promise great power to those who listen. Their cults are scattered and separated, with little to no unity between the greater evils. Hidden hierarchies of power-hungry mortals corrupt and seduce, promising a sliver of the same power they had been promised when the time comes to reap their harvest.
You once belonged to such a cult. Perhaps it was brief, embracing the rebellious spirit of youth and curious where this path may take you. You also may have felt alone and lost, this community offering a welcome you had been subconsciously seeking. It’s possible you were raised from the beginning to pray to the gods of shadow and death. Then one day the veil was lifted and the cruel truth shook your faith, sending you running from the false promises and seeking redemption.
You have been freed from the bindings of these dangerous philosophies, but few secret societies find comfort until those who abandon their way are rotting beneath the soil.

**Languages.** One of your choice.

**Wicked Awareness.** Your time worshipping in secrecy and shadow at the altar of malevolent forces has left you with insight and keen awareness to those who still operate in such ways. You can often spot hidden signs, messages, and signals left in populated places. If actively seeking signs of a cult or dark following, you have an easier time locating and decoding the signs or social interactions that signify cult activity, gaining advantage on any ability checks to discover such details.
gear: Vestments and a holy symbol of your previous cult, a set of common clothes, a belt pouch containing 15 gp.

name: Con Artist
desc:
You have always had a knack for getting people to see your point of view, often to their own detriment. You know how people think, what they want, and how to best use that to your advantage.

People should know better than to trust you when you offer exactly what they need for exactly as much money as they have, but for the desperate caution is a resource in short supply. Your mysterious bottles, unlikely rumors, and secret maps offer to deliver the salvation they need. When they realize they've been had, you're nowhere to be found.

**Tool Proficiencies.** Two of your choice

**Cover Story.** You have created a secondary persona that includes documents, mannerisms, a social presence and acquaintances. This also includes an alternate set of clothing and accessories as well as any elements needed for the disguise such as a wig or false teeth. Additionally, you can duplicate or fake documents-including official documents or personal correspondence-as long as you have seen a similar document and have an appropriate handwriting sample.
gear: A set of fine clothes, a disguise kit, tools for your typical con (such as bottles full of colored water, a set of weighted dice, a deck of marked or filed cards, or a seal from an imaginary-or real-noble), and a pouch containing 15gp

name: Death Domain
desc: A domain of necromancy and death. Source: Dungeon Master’s Guide (2014), pp. 96–97.

features.d: Always prepared by cleric level: 1st — False Life and Ray of Sickness; 3rd — Blindness/Deafness and Ray of Enfeeblement; 5th — Animate Dead and Vampiric Touch; 7th — Blight and Death Ward; 9th — Antilife Shell and Cloudkill.
Gain proficiency with martial weapons.
Learn one necromancy cantrip from any spell list. When a necromancy cantrip normally targets one creature, it can target two in range within 5 feet of each other.
On a melee hit, spend Channel Divinity to deal extra necrotic damage equal to 5 plus twice your cleric level.
Your cleric spells and Channel Divinity ignore resistance to necrotic damage.
Once on your turn on a weapon hit, add 1d8 necrotic damage. At cleric level 14, this becomes 2d8.
A necromancy spell of levels 1–5 that normally targets one creature can target two in range within 5 feet of each other. Supply consumed materials for both targets.

name: Oathbreaker
desc: A fallen paladin option for campaigns that allow villainous subclasses. Source: Dungeon Master’s Guide (2014), pp. 96–97.

features.d: Always prepared by paladin level: 3rd — Hellish Rebuke and Inflict Wounds; 5th — Crown of Madness and Darkness; 9th — Animate Dead and Bestow Curse; 13th — Blight and Confusion; 17th — Contagion and Dominate Person.
As an action, one visible undead within 30 feet makes a Wisdom save. On failure it obeys for 24 hours or until you use this option again. Undead with CR at least your paladin level are immune.

As an action, choose creatures within 30 feet that can see you. On a failed Wisdom save, they are frightened for 1 minute. Affected creatures can save again at the end of turns more than 30 feet away.
You and fiends and undead within 10 feet add your Charisma modifier to melee weapon damage, minimum +1. The radius increases to 30 feet at level 18. A creature can benefit from only one such aura.
Gain resistance to bludgeoning, piercing and slashing damage from nonmagical weapons.

Once per long rest, as an action, create a 30-foot aura for 1 minute. It dims bright light. Frightened enemies starting a turn in it take 4d10 psychic damage. Chosen creatures in the aura gain protection against attacks that rely on sight. As a bonus action make a melee spell attack for 3d10 plus your Charisma modifier necrotic damage.

tools: Thieves’ tools, tinker’s tools, and one type of artisan’s tools
kit: Light crossbow, 20 bolts, Scale mail, Thieves' tools, Dungeoneer's pack

features.d: Imbue tiny objects with minor sensory effects.
Prepare Intelligence-based spells and cast them through tools.
Learn infusions and turn suitable objects into magic items.

features.n: The Right Tool for the Job
features.d: Use your tools to create a set of artisan’s tools.
Double your proficiency bonus on proficient tool checks.
React to boost a nearby ability check or save by your Intelligence modifier.
Attune to four items and craft common or uncommon items faster and more cheaply.
Store a qualifying 1st- or 2nd-level artificer spell in an object for repeated use.
Attune to five items and ignore specified restrictions when using magic items.
Attune to six items.
Gain a save bonus for each attuned item and end an infusion to avoid dropping to 0 HP.

desc: An Intelligence-based spellcaster who uses tools and infusions to create magic items.

name: Alchemist
desc: 2014 Artificer subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything, p. 14.

features.d: Always prepared by class level. Level 3: Healing Word, Ray of Sickness. Level 5: Flaming Sphere, Melf’s Acid Arrow. Level 9: Gaseous Form, Mass Healing Word. Level 13: Blight, Death Ward. Level 17: Cloudkill, Raise Dead.
Make a random elixir after a long rest or spend a slot to choose an effect.
Gain alchemist’s supplies proficiency or another artisan’s tool proficiency if you already have it.
When casting with alchemist’s supplies, add Intelligence to a qualifying healing or damage roll.
Elixirs grant temporary HP and you can cast Lesser Restoration without slots a limited number of times.
Resist acid and poison, gain poison immunity against the condition, and cast Heal and Greater Restoration once each per long rest.

name: Armorer
desc: 2014 Artificer subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything, p. 15.

features.d: Infiltrator armor grants advantage on Stealth that offsets its own disadvantage.
Guardian armor spends a bonus action to grant temporary HP equal to artificer level, with limited uses.
Infiltrator armor fires lightning and deals an extra die on one hit per turn.
Infiltrator armor raises walking speed by 5 feet.
Guardian gauntlets deal thunder damage and hinder the target’s attacks against others.
Turn worn armor into a focus that covers your body and ignores its Strength requirement.
Choose Guardian or Infiltrator and switch after a short or long rest with smith’s tools.

Always prepared by class level. Level 3: Magic Missile, Thunderwave. Level 5: Mirror Image, Shatter. Level 9: Hypnotic Pattern, Lightning Bolt. Level 13: Fire Shield, Greater Invisibility. Level 17: Passwall, Wall of Force.
Gain heavy armor and smith’s tools training, with a substitute tool proficiency if needed.
Attack twice with the Attack action.
Infuse separate pieces of your arcane armor and gain two extra infusions for those pieces.
Pull a nearby creature toward you as a reaction and potentially strike it.
Launcher hits mark foes, hinder their attacks against you and improve the next attack against them.
Your chosen armor model gains an upgraded combat ability.

name: Artillerist
desc: 2014 Artificer subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything, p. 17.

features.d: Always prepared by class level. Level 3: Shield, Thunderwave. Level 5: Scorching Ray, Shatter. Level 9: Fireball, Wind Wall. Level 13: Ice Storm, Wall of Fire. Level 17: Cone of Cold, Wall of Force.
Build a Flamethrower, Force Ballista, or Protector cannon and activate it with a bonus action.
Gain woodcarver’s tools proficiency or another artisan’s tool proficiency if needed.
Carve a focus that adds a d8 to one damage roll of an artificer spell cast through it.
Your cannon deals more damage and can be detonated to deal force damage nearby.
Keep two cannons active and grant nearby allies half cover.

name: Battle Smith
desc: 2014 Artificer subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything, p. 18.

features.d: Gain martial weapon proficiency and use Intelligence with magic weapons.

Always prepared by class level. Level 3: Heroism, Shield. Level 5: Branding Smite, Warding Bond. Level 9: Aura of Vitality, Conjure Barrage. Level 13: Aura of Purity, Fire Shield. Level 17: Banishing Smite, Mass Cure Wounds.
Build a companion that attacks on command and can hinder attacks against others.
Gain smith’s tools proficiency or another artisan’s tool proficiency if needed.
Attack twice with the Attack action.
On a qualifying hit, deal extra force damage or heal a nearby creature or object.
Boost Arcane Jolt and your defender’s armor, and make its defensive reaction damage the attacker.

name: Path of the Ancestral Guardian
desc: 2014 Barbarian subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 9.

features.d: Your first hit while raging hinders the target’s attacks against others and protects those it hits.
While raging, react to reduce damage to another creature nearby.
Cast Augury or Clairvoyance without a slot once per rest.
Spirit Shield deals force damage to the attacker equal to the damage it prevents.

name: Path of the Storm Herald
desc: 2014 Barbarian subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 10.

features.d: Deal fire damage to other creatures in your aura.
Zap one creature in the aura for lightning damage, halved on a successful Dexterity save.
Grant temporary HP to creatures you choose in the aura.
Choose Desert, Sea, or Tundra when gaining a level. Trigger its aura when you rage and as a bonus action later.
Gain fire resistance and adapt to extreme heat.
Gain lightning resistance, underwater breathing, and a swim speed.
Gain cold resistance and adapt to extreme cold.
Gain defenses tied to your chosen environment.
Chosen creatures in your active aura share your Storm Soul damage resistance.
React to a hit against you by burning the attacker if it fails its save.
After hitting a creature in your aura, force a Strength save or knock it prone.
When triggering your aura, try to freeze one creature in place.
Your storm environment adds a new combat effect while raging.

name: Path of the Zealot
desc: 2014 Barbarian subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 11.

features.d: Your first weapon hit each turn while raging deals extra radiant or necrotic damage, chosen when you gain this feature.
Resurrection spells targeting you waive their material component cost.
Once per rage, reroll a failed saving throw.
Once per long rest, give nearby allies advantage on attacks and saves until your next turn.
While raging, 0 HP and failed death saves can delay your death until your rage ends.

name: Path of the Beast
desc: 2014 Barbarian subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything, p. 24.

features.d: When raging, manifest a healing bite, extra-attacking claws, or a defensive tail.
Your natural weapons become magical. After a rest choose improved swimming, climbing, or jumping.
A natural weapon hit can force the target to strike another creature or take psychic damage.
When starting a rage, gain temporary HP and let chosen allies add damage to a hit each turn.

name: Path of Wild Magic
desc: 2014 Barbarian subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything, p. 25.

features.d: Sense nearby spells and magic items a limited number of times per long rest.
Roll on a magical effects table whenever you enter a rage.
Give a creature a bonus to attacks and checks or recover one low-level spell slot.
After taking damage or failing a save while raging, react to roll a replacement surge.
Roll twice for each surge and choose the result, or pick any effect on doubles.

name: College of Glamour
desc: 2014 Bard subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 14.

features.d: After performing, charm members of your audience who fail a Wisdom save.
Spend Bardic Inspiration to give allies temporary HP and let them move without provoking.
For one minute, cast Command as a bonus action without slots.
For one minute, attackers must pass a Charisma save to attack you for the first time each turn.

name: College of Swords
desc: 2014 Bard subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 15.

features.d: Add an inspiration die to damage and AC.
Add an inspiration die to damage, push the target back, and move after it.
Add the die to damage dealt to the target and nearby creatures of your choice.
Attacking increases your walking speed. On a qualifying hit, spend inspiration on one flourish per turn.
Gain medium armor and scimitar proficiency and use a proficient melee weapon as a focus.
Choose Dueling or Two-Weapon Fighting.
Attack twice with the Attack action.
Use a d6 for a flourish without spending Bardic Inspiration.

name: College of Whispers
desc: 2014 Bard subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 16.

features.d: Spend Bardic Inspiration to deal extra psychic damage on a weapon hit.
After speaking with a humanoid privately, potentially frighten it for an hour.
Capture a dying humanoid’s shadow and use it to impersonate them.
Charm a creature with a whispered threat and gain its fearful cooperation.

name: College of Creation
desc: 2014 Bard subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything, p. 28.

features.d: Inspiration grants an additional benefit depending on whether it boosts a check, attack, or save.
Create a temporary nonmagical object within a size and price limit.
Animate an object as a dancing ally and command it with a bonus action.
Create several objects at once and ignore the price limit.

name: College of Eloquence

features.d: Treat a d20 roll below 10 as 10 for Persuasion and Deception.
Spend Bardic Inspiration to subtract its roll from a creature’s next save.
A creature keeps your inspiration die when it spends it but still fails.
Make your speech understandable to chosen creatures for an hour.
When a creature succeeds with your inspiration, pass a new die to another creature as a reaction.

name: Forge Domain

features.d: After a long rest, make one nonmagical suit of armor or weapon magical with a +1 bonus.
Gain heavy armor and smith’s tools proficiency.
Use a ritual and metal of equal value to create a qualifying object worth at most 100 gp.
Resist fire and gain +1 AC in heavy armor.
Add fire damage to one weapon hit per turn.
Gain fire immunity and resist nonmagical weapon damage while wearing heavy armor.

name: Grave Domain
desc: 2014 Cleric subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 19.

Sense nearby undead that are outside total cover.

features.n: Channel Divinity: Path to the Grave
features.d: Make a creature vulnerable to all damage from the next attack that hits it.
Turn a nearby critical hit into a normal hit as a reaction.
Add your Wisdom modifier to cleric cantrip damage.
When an enemy dies nearby, restore HP to yourself or an ally.

When you target an ally with a leveled spell, let one ally react to make a weapon attack.
Charm chosen creatures nearby and optionally make them drop what they hold.
Cast eligible enchantment spells as bonus actions a limited number of times.
Deal extra psychic damage on one weapon hit per turn.
Your Divine Strike can mark a foe for extra psychic damage from an ally’s next hit.

name: Peace Domain

Move without provoking and heal creatures you pass once each.
A bonded creature can teleport to take damage for another bonded creature.

Extend the bond’s working range and grant resistance to damage intercepted with Protective Bond.

name: Twilight Domain
desc: 2014 Cleric subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything, p. 34.

features.d: Gain martial weapons and heavy armor proficiency.
Gain 300-foot darkvision and temporarily share it with allies.
Give a creature advantage on its next initiative roll.
Create moving dim light that can grant temporary HP or end charm or fear at the end of a creature’s turn.
Gain temporary flight while in dim light or darkness.
Deal extra radiant damage on one weapon hit per turn.
You and allies gain half cover inside Twilight Sanctuary.

name: Circle of Dreams

name: Circle of the Shepherd

name: Circle of Spores

features.d: Learn Chill Touch and always prepare fungus-themed spells at the listed levels.

Gain immunity to several conditions and prevent critical hits unless incapacitated.

name: Circle of Stars
desc: 2014 Druid subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything, p. 38.

features.d: Use a star map as a focus, learn Guidance, and cast Guiding Bolt for free a limited number of times.
Spend Wild Shape to take the Archer, Chalice, or Dragon form.
Make a ranged radiant spell attack when you activate the form and as a bonus action later.
When you spend a slot healing, also heal yourself or a nearby creature.
Treat low rolls on Intelligence, Wisdom, and concentration checks as 10.
After a long rest, roll for whether you can add or subtract a d6 from nearby rolls as a reaction.
Improve all three forms, give Dragon flight, and switch forms at the start of your turns.
Resist bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage in Starry Form.

name: Circle of Wildfire
desc: 2014 Druid subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything, p. 39.

features.d: Always prepare fire and healing spells as you advance.
Spend Wild Shape to summon a spirit that attacks and teleports allies.
While your spirit is active, boost fire or healing rolls and cast eligible spells from its space.
Use flames left by fallen creatures to heal or burn someone.
Sacrifice your active spirit to survive being reduced to 0 HP once per long rest.

name: Arcane Archer
desc: 2014 Fighter subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 28.

features.d: Choose Arcana or Nature proficiency and learn Prestidigitation or Druidcraft.
Imbue a qualifying bow shot with magic, twice per short or long rest.
Learn two arcane shots from Banishing, Beguiling, Bursting, Enfeebling, Grasping, Piercing, Seeking, and Shadow Arrow.
Learn another Arcane Shot option.
After a missed magical arrow, use a bonus action to try hitting a different nearby target.
Your ordinary arrows from a shortbow or longbow can count as magical.
Learn another Arcane Shot option.
Learn another Arcane Shot option.
Regain one use when rolling initiative with none remaining.
Learn another Arcane Shot option and improve your shots’ effects.

name: Cavalier
desc: 2014 Fighter subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 30.

features.d: Choose Animal Handling, History, Insight, Performance, Persuasion, or a language.
Mount quickly, resist being dismounted, and land safely on certain falls.
Mark a creature you hit, hinder its attacks against others nearby, and punish it with a limited bonus-action attack.
React to add a d8 to AC for a nearby target and grant resistance to the triggering damage if the attack still hits.
Enemies provoke when moving within your reach, and your opportunity hits stop their movement.
After a straight charge, a melee hit can knock a target prone.
Gain a separate opportunity-attack reaction on each other creature’s turn.

name: Samurai
desc: 2014 Fighter subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 31.

features.d: Choose History, Insight, Performance, Persuasion, or a language.
Use a bonus action to gain temporary HP and advantage on weapon attacks for the turn.
Add Wisdom to Persuasion checks and gain Wisdom save proficiency or a substitute.
Regain one Fighting Spirit use when rolling initiative with none left.
Trade advantage on one attack for an extra attack against the same target once per turn.
React to taking damage to 0 HP by taking a turn before falling unconscious.

name: Psi Warrior
desc: 2014 Fighter subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything, p. 42.

features.d: Use a psionic die to reduce damage to yourself or a nearby creature.
Spend a die to deal extra force damage after a qualifying weapon hit.
Move a loose object or willing creature telekinetically, with the first use free each rest.
Gain psionic dice that scale with level and return on a long rest.
Gain a flying speed of twice your walking speed for the turn.
A creature hit by Psionic Strike can be pushed or knocked prone on a failed save.
Gain Psi-Powered Leap and Telekinetic Thrust.
Resist psychic damage and spend a die to end charm or fear on yourself.
Give chosen creatures half cover for up to one minute.
Cast Telekinesis with Intelligence and make a weapon attack as a bonus action while concentrating on it.

name: Rune Knight
desc: 2014 Fighter subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything, p. 44.

features.d: Gain smith’s tools proficiency and learn Giant.
Become Large when space allows, gain Strength advantage and add damage to one hit per turn.
Inscribe objects with learned runes that confer passive benefits and can be invoked for a stronger effect.
Learn another rune.
React to force an attack against a nearby creature to be rerolled.
Learn another rune.
Grow taller and increase Giant’s Might damage to a d8.
Learn another rune.
Invoke each rune twice per short or long rest.
Giant’s Might damage becomes a d10 and you can grow Huge with extra reach.

name: Way of the Drunken Master
desc: 2014 Monk subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 33.

features.d: Gain Performance and brewer’s supplies proficiency.
Flurry of Blows grants Disengage and 10 extra feet of walking speed that turn.
Stand from prone by spending only 5 feet of movement.
Spend ki to redirect a missed melee attack to another creature nearby.
Gain Leap to Your Feet and Redirect Attack.
Spend two ki to cancel disadvantage on an attack, ability check, or save.
Flurry of Blows can make up to three additional attacks if each Flurry attack targets a different creature.

name: Way of the Kensei
desc: 2014 Monk subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 34.

features.d: While holding a melee kensei weapon, gain +2 AC after an unarmed strike as part of your Attack action.
Use a bonus action to add 1d4 damage to ranged kensei weapon hits that turn.
Choose one melee and one ranged kensei weapon and gain calligrapher’s or painter’s supplies proficiency.
Your kensei weapons count as magical and can spend ki to add a Martial Arts die to damage once per turn.
Spend up to three ki as a bonus action for a matching bonus to a qualifying weapon’s attack and damage rolls.
Reroll one missed monk weapon attack per turn.

name: Way of the Sun Soul
desc: 2014 Monk subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 35.

features.d: Fire radiant bolts using Dexterity and your Martial Arts die. Spend ki after using the bolts to fire two more as a bonus action.
After taking the Attack action, spend ki to cast Burning Hands as a bonus action.
Launch a sphere that deals radiant damage on a failed save, spending ki to increase the damage.
Emit light and retaliate with radiant damage when hit by a melee attack while it shines.

name: Way of Mercy
desc: 2014 Monk subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything, p. 49.

features.d: Spend ki on an unarmed hit for extra necrotic damage, once per turn.
Spend ki to heal a creature you touch, or replace a Flurry of Blows strike with healing.
Gain Insight, Medicine, and herbalism kit proficiency.
Your healing can end an eligible condition or disease and Hand of Harm can poison its target.
Apply healing to both Flurry strikes or use Hand of Harm with a Flurry hit without extra ki.
Spend ki to revive a creature that died within the past 24 hours, once per long rest.

name: Way of the Astral Self
desc: 2014 Monk subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything, p. 50.

features.d: Spend ki to summon spectral arms with extra reach that strike using Wisdom and deal force damage.
Spend ki for enhanced vision, social checks, and control over how far your voice carries.
While arms and visage are active, deflect certain energy damage and add damage to an astral arm strike.
Manifest the complete form for an AC bonus and a third astral arm attack when attacking twice with the arms.

name: Oath of Conquest
desc: 2014 Paladin subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 37.

features.d: Choose Conquering Presence or Guided Strike when spending your Channel Divinity.
Frighten chosen creatures nearby that fail a Wisdom save.
Add +10 to your attack roll after seeing the roll and before knowing the outcome.

Always prepared by class level. Level 3: Armor of Agathys, Command. Level 5: Hold Person, Spiritual Weapon. Level 9: Bestow Curse, Fear. Level 13: Dominate Beast, Stoneskin. Level 17: Cloudkill, Dominate Person.
Crush opposition, rule firmly, and prove your strength.
A creature frightened of you has zero speed and takes psychic damage when it starts its turn in your aura.
Damage attackers with psychic energy when they hit you.
For one minute, resist all damage, gain another attack, and score weapon critical hits on 19 or 20.

name: Oath of Redemption
desc: 2014 Paladin subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 38.

features.d: Choose Emissary of Peace or Rebuke the Violent when spending your Channel Divinity.
Gain +5 to Persuasion checks for 10 minutes.

Always prepared by class level. Level 3: Sanctuary, Sleep. Level 5: Calm Emotions, Hold Person. Level 9: Counterspell, Hypnotic Pattern. Level 13: Otiluke’s Resilient Sphere, Stoneskin. Level 17: Hold Monster, Wall of Force.
React to a nearby attacker hurting someone else and reflect radiant damage, halved on a successful Wisdom save.
Seek peace, protect innocence, practice patience, and choose force with care.
React to take damage in place of a nearby creature.
Regain hit points at the end of your turn when below half HP if you can act.
Resist damage from a creature and reflect part of it, losing that protection against a creature you attack or harm until your next long rest.

name: Oath of Glory
desc: 2014 Paladin subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything, p. 53.

features.d: Choose Inspiring Smite or Peerless Athlete when spending your Channel Divinity.

Always prepared by class level. Level 3: Guiding Bolt, Heroism. Level 5: Enhance Ability, Magic Weapon. Level 9: Haste, Protection from Energy. Level 13: Compulsion, Freedom of Movement. Level 17: Commune, Flame Strike.
Prove yourself through deeds, face challenges, and build discipline.
After Divine Smite, distribute temporary HP among chosen creatures nearby.
Improve Athletics and Acrobatics, carrying capacity, and jumping for ten minutes.
Move 10 feet faster and boost the speed of allies that start their turn in your aura.
React to improve AC against one hit for yourself or an ally, and possibly counterattack.
Temporarily improve Charisma checks and gain limited rerolls for attacks and saving throws.

name: Oath of the Watchers
desc: 2014 Paladin subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything, p. 54.

features.d: Choose Abjure the Extraplanar or Watcher’s Will when spending your Channel Divinity.

Always prepared by class level. Level 3: Alarm, Detect Magic. Level 5: Moonbeam, See Invisibility. Level 9: Counterspell, Nondetection. Level 13: Aura of Purity, Banishment. Level 17: Hold Monster, Scrying.
Stay vigilant, loyal, and disciplined against extraplanar threats.
Turn selected creature types from beyond the mortal realm.
Give chosen allies advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saves for one minute.
Add your proficiency bonus to initiative for yourself and nearby allies.
React to a successful mental save by dealing force damage to its source.
Gain truesight and advantage against certain extraplanar creatures. Hits can banish a creature that fails a Charisma save.

name: Gloom Stalker
desc: 2014 Ranger subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 41.

features.d: Add Wisdom to initiative. On your first turn, move faster and make an extra attack with bonus damage when you take the Attack action.
Learn Disguise Self, Rope Trick, Fear, Greater Invisibility, and Seeming at ranger levels 3, 5, 9, 13, and 17.
Gain darkvision or extend it, and remain unseen by creatures relying on darkvision in darkness.
Gain Wisdom save proficiency, or choose Intelligence or Charisma if you already have it.
Once on each of your turns, make another weapon attack after you miss with one.
React to impose disadvantage on an attack that otherwise has no advantage.

name: Horizon Walker
desc: 2014 Ranger subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 42.

features.d: Sense the direction and distance of the nearest planar portal within one mile.
Learn Protection from Evil and Good, Misty Step, Haste, Banishment, and Teleportation Circle at ranger levels 3, 5, 9, 13, and 17.
Mark a nearby target as a bonus action. Your next weapon hit that turn becomes force damage and deals bonus damage.
Use a bonus action to enter the Ethereal Plane until your turn ends.
Teleport before attacks and gain a third attack against a different target after attacking two distinct creatures.
React to gain resistance to all damage from a hit.

name: Monster Slayer
desc: 2014 Ranger subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 43.

features.d: Learn a creature’s damage immunities, resistances, and vulnerabilities unless concealed by magic.
Learn Protection from Evil and Good, Zone of Truth, Magic Circle, Banishment, and Hold Monster at ranger levels 3, 5, 9, 13, and 17.
Mark a creature as a bonus action and add damage to the first weapon hit against it each turn.
Add a d6 to saves or grapple escape checks caused by your marked prey.
React to potentially stop a spell or teleport with a Wisdom save.
React with a weapon attack when your prey forces a save. A hit automatically succeeds on the save.

name: Fey Wanderer

features.d: Deal bonus psychic damage to each creature you hit with a weapon, once per target per turn.
Learn Charm Person, Misty Step, Dispel Magic, Dimension Door, and Mislead at ranger levels 3, 5, 9, 13, and 17.
Add Wisdom to Charisma checks and choose Deception, Performance, or Persuasion proficiency.
Gain advantage against charm and fear and react to redirect either effect when a save succeeds.
Learn Summon Fey and cast it without components or a slot once per long rest, optionally without concentration for one minute.
Cast Misty Step without slots a limited number of times and bring a willing creature.

name: Swarmkeeper
desc: 2014 Ranger subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything, p. 59.

features.d: Once per turn after a hit, choose extra piercing damage, move the target on a failed Strength save, or move yourself.
Learn Mage Hand and gain Faerie Fire, Web, Gaseous Form, Arcane Eye, and Insect Plague at ranger levels 3, 5, 9, 13, and 17.
Gain a temporary flying speed with hover.
Improve swarm damage and knock the target prone or gain half cover with the appropriate swarm movement.
React to resist triggering damage and teleport up to 30 feet.

name: Inquisitive
desc: 2014 Rogue subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 45.

features.d: Treat rolls below 8 as 8 for Insight checks to detect lies.
Use a bonus action to look for a hidden creature or object, or inspect a clue.
Contest Insight against Deception to gain Sneak Attack against that target without advantage unless you have disadvantage.
Gain advantage on Perception and Investigation when moving no more than half your speed.
Sense nearby deception from illusions or transformed creatures.
Deal an extra 3d6 Sneak Attack damage to a creature under Insightful Fighting.

name: Mastermind
desc: 2014 Rogue subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 46.

features.d: Gain disguise kit, forgery kit, and a gaming set proficiency, two languages, and the ability to mimic speech patterns.
Use Help as a bonus action and aid attacks against targets within 30 feet that can see or hear you.
Study a creature to compare selected mental abilities or class levels with yours.
Redirect an attack aimed at you to a creature providing cover.
Block involuntary thought reading and deceive magic that would determine whether you’re telling the truth.

name: Scout
desc: 2014 Rogue subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 47.

features.d: React to move half your speed without provoking when an enemy ends its turn next to you.
Gain Nature and Survival proficiency and double your proficiency bonus on those checks.
Increase walking speed by 10 feet, also applying to any climbing or swimming speed you have.
Gain initiative advantage and give allies advantage against the first target you hit in round one.
After taking the Attack action, make a bonus-action attack that can Sneak Attack a second target.

name: Swashbuckler
desc: 2014 Rogue subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 48.

features.d: A creature you make a melee attack against cannot make opportunity attacks against you that turn.
Add Charisma to initiative and gain Sneak Attack in qualifying one-on-one fights.
Contest Persuasion against Insight to distract a hostile creature or charm a nonhostile one briefly.
Use a bonus action to gain advantage on your next Athletics or Acrobatics check that turn.
After a miss, reroll the attack with advantage once per short or long rest.

name: Phantom
desc: 2014 Rogue subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything, p. 62.

features.d: After Sneak Attack, deal psychic damage to another nearby target a limited number of times.
After a rest, choose a temporary skill or tool proficiency.
Capture departing souls in tokens for survival benefits, bonus Wails uses, or one question of the dead.
Become spectral, fly slowly, and move through creatures and objects.
Wails can damage your Sneak Attack target as well, and you gain a token on a long rest if you have none.

name: Soulknife
desc: 2014 Rogue subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything, p. 63.

features.d: Spend a die after failing a proficient check, expending it only if the check succeeds.
Link telepathically to chosen creatures for hours determined by a psionic die.
Gain psionic dice that scale with your level and fuel subclass abilities.
Manifest a psychic finesse blade with 60-foot range and a weaker bonus-action blade.
Add a psionic die to a missed blade attack, spending it only if you hit.
Throw a psychic blade to teleport up to ten times the die roll in feet.
Gain Homing Strikes and Psychic Teleportation.
Become invisible for an hour or until you deal damage or force a save.
After a psychic-blade Sneak Attack, force a Wisdom save or stun the target.

name: Divine Soul
desc: 2014 Sorcerer subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 50.

features.d: Choose from the cleric or sorcerer spell list and gain a bonus spell tied to your divine affinity.
Add 2d4 after missing an attack or failing a save once per short or long rest.
Spend a sorcery point to reroll healing dice for a nearby spell.
Manifest spectral wings and fly up to 30 feet per turn.
As a bonus action while below half HP, recover half your maximum HP once per long rest.

name: Shadow Magic
desc: 2014 Sorcerer subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 50.

features.d: Gain 120-foot darkvision and learn Darkness at level 3. You can see through it when you cast it with sorcery points.
When reduced to 0 HP, try a Charisma save to drop to 1 HP instead, with exceptions for radiant damage and critical hits.
Spend sorcery points to summon a hound that pursues a chosen target and hinders its saves against your spells.
Teleport between areas of dim light or darkness as a bonus action.
Spend sorcery points to become shadowy, resisting most damage and moving through creatures and objects.

name: Storm Sorcery
desc: 2014 Sorcerer subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 51.

features.d: Before or after casting a leveled spell, fly 10 feet without provoking as a bonus action.
Learn Primordial and communicate with its elemental dialects.
Resist lightning and thunder and damage nearby chosen creatures when casting spells of either type.
Stop rain around you or direct nearby wind for a round.
React to a melee hit with lightning damage and potentially push the attacker away.
Gain immunity to lightning and thunder, fly, and temporarily share flight with allies.

name: Aberrant Mind
desc: 2014 Sorcerer subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything, p. 66.

features.d: Learn bonus psionic spells and replace eligible ones on leveling with qualifying divination or enchantment spells.
Link telepathically to a nearby creature for minutes equal to your sorcerer level.
Cast bonus psionic spells with sorcery points to bypass most components.
Resist psychic damage and gain advantage against charm and fear.
Spend sorcery points for flight, swimming, seeing invisible creatures, or squeezing through tight openings.
Teleport and force nearby creatures at your departure space to save against force damage and a pull.

name: Clockwork Soul
desc: 2014 Sorcerer subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything, p. 68.

features.d: Learn extra spells and replace eligible ones on leveling with qualifying abjuration or transmutation spells.
React to cancel advantage or disadvantage on a nearby roll, with uses based on proficiency bonus.
Spend sorcery points to ward a creature with d8s it can expend to reduce damage.
For one minute, attacks against you cannot gain advantage and your d20 rolls below 10 count as 10.
In a cube near you, distribute up to 100 healing, repair objects, and end eligible spells.

name: The Celestial
desc: 2014 Warlock subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 54.

features.d: Learn Light and Sacred Flame without using your normal cantrip allowance.
Spend d6s from a pool as a bonus action to heal a creature within 60 feet.
Resist radiant damage and add Charisma to a radiant or fire damage roll against one spell target.
After a rest, grant temporary HP to yourself and up to five other creatures.
Instead of making a death save, regain half your HP, stand, and deal radiant damage and blindness to nearby enemies.

name: The Hexblade
desc: 2014 Warlock subclass from Xanathar’s Guide to Everything, p. 55.

features.d: Gain medium armor, shields, and martial weapons and attack with Charisma using an eligible weapon.
Curse a nearby creature as a bonus action for bonus damage, expanded critical range, and healing when it dies.
Bind a specter to your service from a humanoid you slay.
React after your cursed target hits you to make the attack miss on a d6 roll of 4 or higher.
Move your curse to another creature after its target dies, giving up the healing.

name: The Fathomless
desc: 2014 Warlock subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything, p. 72.

features.d: Gain a 40-foot swim speed and breathe underwater.
Summon a tentacle that attacks and slows targets, then move and attack with it on later turns.
React to reduce damage dealt to a creature near your tentacle.
Resist cold and communicate with submerged creatures while underwater.
Learn Evard’s Black Tentacles, cast it without a slot once per long rest, and gain temporary HP and protected concentration when casting it.
Teleport yourself and willing creatures to a known body of water within one mile.

name: The Genie
desc: 2014 Warlock subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything, p. 73.

features.d: Enter your vessel and shelter inside until your time limit expires or you leave.
Once during your turn, add damage of your patron type to a hit.
Choose Dao, Djinni, Efreeti, or Marid and receive a vessel usable as a focus.
Resist your patron’s damage type and gain limited bonus-action flight.
Bring allies into the vessel and gain short-rest benefits in ten minutes, with extra healing from Hit Dice.
Request the effect of a spell of up to 6th level with a casting time of one action, then recharge after 1d4 long rests.

name: War Magic
desc: React to a hit or failed save for +2 AC or +4 to the save, limiting your next turn’s spells to cantrips.

features.d: React to a hit or failed save for +2 AC or +4 to the save, limiting your next turn’s spells to cantrips.

Store surges through successful Counterspell or Dispel Magic and spend them to add force damage.

name: Bladesinging
desc: 2014 Wizard subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything, p. 76.

features.d: Use a bonus action to gain enhanced AC, movement, acrobatics, and concentration while meeting weapon and armor restrictions.
Gain light armor, one type of one-handed melee weapon, and Performance proficiency.
Attack twice with the Attack action and replace one attack with a cantrip.
Spend a spell slot as a reaction to reduce damage during Bladesong.
Add Intelligence to melee weapon damage while Bladesong is active.

name: Order of Scribes
desc: 2014 Wizard subclass from Tasha’s Cauldron of Everything, p. 77.

Summon a quill that needs no ink and copies spells faster.
Manifest your spellbook’s mind and cast a limited number of spells from its location.
Make a temporary scroll from an eligible spell and copy spell scrolls faster and more cheaply.
Prevent damage by temporarily losing spells from your book, and gain advantage on Arcana checks while the mind is present.

features.d: Prepare a fixed number of Intelligence-based spells. Cast them using a proficient tool as a focus, and replace one cantrip after a long rest.
Learn Mending and use tinker’s tools to create temporary mundane gear.
Learn blueprints at qualifying levels and use them after a long rest to create magic items.
Recharge a replicated item with a slot, reclaim a slot from one, or trade it for another plan.

name: Death Knight
desc: A World of Warcraft class using the revised Paladin progression and its Azeroth subclass options.

features.d: Your creature type becomes Undead. You have a long-rest pool of d8s equal to 1 + your Charisma modifier (minimum 1). As a bonus action, spend up to your Charisma modifier in dice (minimum 1) on a visible creature within 60 feet. It makes a Constitution save against your spell DC and takes the roll as Necrotic damage, halved on a success. You can instead heal an Undead target by the rolled amount.
Rune Strike is always prepared. One casting per long rest is free.

Find Steed is always prepared and can be cast once per long rest without a slot. You can choose an Undead steed with a Necrotic slam. Once per long rest, it can use a bonus action to move itself and its rider through objects or creatures as difficult terrain for that turn. Both take 1d10 Force damage if they end their turn inside an object.
A hit with a melee weapon or unarmed strike adds 1d8 Necrotic damage.
Damage from Death Coil increases by your Charisma modifier (minimum 1) regardless of the save. When healing an Undead creature instead, add your Death Knight level.

name: Oath of the Ebon Blade
desc: Choose a Blood, Frost, or Unholy rune and imbue your weapon with its power.

features.n: Oath of the Ebon Blade Spells
features.d: Always prepare the shared spells and those from your selected specialization. All: level 3 Death Grip, level 5 Death and Decay, level 9 Summon Undead, level 13 Freedom of Movement, level 17 Circle of Power; Blood: level 3 Vampiric Blood, level 5 Spiritual Weapon, level 9 Leeching Strike, level 13 Evard's Black Tentacles, level 17 Bonestorm; Frost: level 3 Chains of Ice, level 5 Frostscythe, level 9 Remorseless Winter, level 13 Ice Storm, level 17 Cone of Cold; Unholy: level 3 Scourge Strike, level 5 Ray of Enfeeblement, level 9 Bestow Curse, level 13 Blight, level 17 Contagion.
Inscribe a melee weapon after a long rest with Blood, Frost, or Unholy. You can transfer the rune after a long rest or switch it at level-up. Your rune also determines your bonus prepared spells.

After casting Rune Strike you may spend Channel Divinity. Blood heals you for the spell’s Necrotic damage. Frost deals 2d6 Cold to the target and enemies within 10 feet of it. Unholy curses the target, subtracting 1d6 from its next save before the end of your next turn.
You and allies inside your Aura of Protection have resistance to Cold, Necrotic, and Psychic damage.
Once per long rest, invoke the power of your inscribed rune. See the rune-specific options in World of Warcraft.

As a bonus action, empower your runes for 10 minutes. Pick any rune effect when using Runic Power or Runic Mastery. Restore Runic Mastery with a level 4 slot. Recharge this aspect on a long rest or with a level 5 slot.

name: Demon Hunter
desc: A World of Warcraft class using the revised Ranger progression and its Azeroth subclass options.

features.d: Prepare spells from this class’s spell list. Your slots return on a long rest.
Gain Expertise in one skill you already know and learn two Azeroth languages.
Choose a Fighting Style feat, Druidic Warrior, or Void Warrior.
Gain Truesight out to 30 feet.

name: Demon Hunter
desc: Use harvested soul fragments to power supernatural attacks.

features.d: Always prepare the shared spells and those from your selected specialization. All: level 3 Throw Glaive, level 5 Sigil of Flame, level 9 Metamorphosis, level 13 Chaos Nova, level 17 Destructive Wave; Devourer: level 3 Consume Soul, level 5 Misty Step, level 9 Soul Reap, level 13 Collapsing Star, level 17 Steel Wind Strike; Havoc: level 3 Fel Rush, level 5 Eye Beam, level 9 Blink, level 13 Fire Shield, level 17 Conjure Volley; Vengeance: level 3 Infernal Strike, level 5 Fiery Brand, level 9 Demon Spikes, level 13 Banishment, level 17 Sigil of Chains.
Spend one soul fragment to cast Feather Fall or Jump without a slot.

Once on your turn when attacking, spend a soul fragment and replace an attack. Each creature within a 10-foot emanation must make a Dexterity save. On failure it takes 1d12 plus your Wisdom modifier Psychic damage and you heal your Wisdom modifier.

On a long rest replenish fragments equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1), plus one at level 13 and a second at level 17. Fragments are Tiny crystals that return to you when more than 30 feet away. Their powers use your spell save DC.
Gain Blindsight out to 10 feet.

Your Hunter’s Mark target has disadvantage on attacks against creatures other than you. Once a turn, when you hit it with a weapon or spell attack, either deal an extra 1d8 Fire damage or subtract 1d4 from its next save before the end of your next turn.
Spend two soul fragments to cast Counterspell as a reaction to its usual trigger.
Spend one soul fragment to cast Throw Glaive as a bonus action without a spell slot.
Gain the Disrupt and Warglaive Mastery soul fragment abilities.
Soul Cleave deals 2d12 plus Wisdom modifier Psychic damage. Regain one soul fragment when you roll initiative with none left.
